questions.question: Describe the properties and classification of proteins.
questions.solution_html:
• Classification
  • Based on source of protein: ((2 marks))
  • Animal protein: derived from animal sources
  • Plant protein: derived from plant source.
  • Based on shape of protein molecule: ((2 marks))
  • Fibrous protein: resemble long ribbons or fibresin shape. Eg. Keratin, collagen
  • Globular protein: possess a spherical or ovoid shape. Eg. Hemoglobin, myoglobin
  • Based on functions: ((4 marks))
  • Defence proteins: defend or protect . eg. Antibodies
  • Contractile proteins: ability to contract. Eg. Actin, myosin
  • Transport proteins: transport of esstential factors. Eg. Hemoglobin, lipoproteins
  • Structural proteins: cell wall and structural component. Eg. Collagen, fibroin
  • Enzymic proteins: catalytic activity. Eg. Urease, amylase
  • Nutrient proteins : act as nutrient. Eg. Ovalbumin, casein
  • storage proteins: storage of nutrients. Eg. Ferritin
  • regulatory proteins: regulatory action. eg. insulin and growth hormone
  • toxic proteins: some proteins are toxic substances. Eg. Snake venom
  • On the basis of composition and solubility: ((2 marks))
  • Simple proteins: yield only amino acids on hydrolysis. Eg. Protamines, histones
  • albumins
  • Conjugate proteins: In addition to amino acids, contain a non-protein group. Eg.
  • Nucleoproteins, mucoproteins, chromoproteins, phosphoproteins, lipoproteins
  • metalloproteins.
  • Derived proteins: formed from simple and conjugate
  • Primary derived: heat, x-ray, acid , alkali. Eg. Proteans, metaproteins
  • Secondary derived: hydrolysis of proteins. Eg. Proteoses, peptones
questions.final_answer: Secondary derived: hydrolysis of proteins. Eg. Proteoses, peptones
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the biological function of Folic acid
questions.solution_html:
•  Vitamin B9, water soluble vitamin ((1 mark))
  •  Folate is crucial for DNA synthesis, repair, and methylation, playing a key role in cell
  • division and growth, especially in rapidly dividing tissues.
  •  It is involved in the synthesis of nucleotides (building blocks of DNA and RNA) and
  • amino acids.
  •  It helps in the conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine
  •  Synthesis of purine and pyramidine bases needed for the synthesis of DNA and RNA
  •  Folate helps in the formation of red and white blood cells in the bone marrow.
  •  It works closely with vitamin B12 in maintaining homocysteine levels, reducing the
  • risk of cardiovascular diseases.
  •  It is especially important during pregnancy for fetal development, as it helps prevent
  • neural tube defects. ((7 marks))
  • Properties: ((2 marks))
  • Folate is water-soluble, and excess amounts are excreted in urine.
  • I is sensitive to heat, light, and oxidation, meaning some folate can be lost during
  • cooking and food processing.

  • position (position 1).This ring has five carbons and one nitrogen atom, with
  • alternating single and double bonds, giving it aromatic stability.
  •  It consists of Hydroxymethyl Group (-CH,OH): Attached to carbon 4 of the
  • pyridine ring, then a Methyl Group (-CH3): Attached to carbon 2 of the ring. And
  • hydroxyl Group (-OH): Attached to carbon 3 of the ring. Together, these groups
  • give pyridoxine its distinctive structure and biochemical properties.
  •  The active coenzyme form of vitamin B6 is pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) ((4 marks))
  •  Structure ((2marks))
  • Properties: ((4 marks))
  • • Vitamin B6 is water-soluble, and excess amounts are excreted in the urine.

questions.question: Describe the properties and classification of proteins.
questions.solution_html:
• Classification
  • Based on source of protein: ((2 marks))
  • Animal protein: derived from animal sources
  • Plant protein: derived from plant source.
  • Based on shape of protein molecule: ((2 marks))
  • Fibrous protein: resemble long ribbons or fibresin shape. Eg. Keratin, collagen
  • Globular protein: possess a spherical or ovoid shape. Eg. Hemoglobin, myoglobin
  • Based on functions: ((4 marks))
  • Defence proteins: defend or protect . eg. Antibodies
  • Contractile proteins: ability to contract. Eg. Actin, myosin
  • Transport proteins: transport of esstential factors. Eg. Hemoglobin, lipoproteins
  • Structural proteins: cell wall and structural component. Eg. Collagen, fibroin
  • Enzymic proteins: catalytic activity. Eg. Urease, amylase
  • Nutrient proteins : act as nutrient. Eg. Ovalbumin, casein
  • storage proteins: storage of nutrients. Eg. Ferritin
  • regulatory proteins: regulatory action. eg. insulin and growth hormone
  • toxic proteins: some proteins are toxic substances. Eg. Snake venom
  • On the basis of composition and solubility: ((2 marks))
  • Simple proteins: yield only amino acids on hydrolysis. Eg. Protamines, histones
  • albumins
  • Conjugate proteins: In addition to amino acids, contain a non-protein group. Eg.
  • Nucleoproteins, mucoproteins, chromoproteins, phosphoproteins, lipoproteins
  • metalloproteins.
  • Derived proteins: formed from simple and conjugate
  • Primary derived: heat, x-ray, acid , alkali. Eg. Proteans, metaproteins
  • Secondary derived: hydrolysis of proteins. Eg. Proteoses, peptones
questions.final_answer: Secondary derived: hydrolysis of proteins. Eg. Proteoses, peptones

questions.question: Explain the biological function of Folic acid
questions.solution_html:
•  Vitamin B9, water soluble vitamin ((1 mark))
  •  Folate is crucial for DNA synthesis, repair, and methylation, playing a key role in cell
  • division and growth, especially in rapidly dividing tissues.
  •  It is involved in the synthesis of nucleotides (building blocks of DNA and RNA) and
  • amino acids.
  •  It helps in the conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine
  •  Synthesis of purine and pyramidine bases needed for the synthesis of DNA and RNA
  •  Folate helps in the formation of red and white blood cells in the bone marrow.
  •  It works closely with vitamin B12 in maintaining homocysteine levels, reducing the
  • risk of cardiovascular diseases.
  •  It is especially important during pregnancy for fetal development, as it helps prevent
  • neural tube defects. ((7 marks))
  • Properties: ((2 marks))
  • Folate is water-soluble, and excess amounts are excreted in urine.
  • I is sensitive to heat, light, and oxidation, meaning some folate can be lost during
  • cooking and food processing.
